system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

content.text:
# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: forklift licence
G2: supermarket or self-service packaging experience (tray sealer, labelling scales)
G3: master butcher qualification (majstorski ispit not passed)
G4: HACCP team leader or advanced HACCP course
G5: unrestricted shift availability (needs the early shift on Wednesdays)

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Claiming a forklift licence or forklift experience because the ad lists it
T2: Calling him a master butcher or listing the majstorski ispit as passed
T3: Inventing supermarket, self-service packing, tray-sealer or labelling-scale experience
T4: Promising full availability for every shift and every Saturday when he needs the early shift on Wednesdays
T5: Old cover letter is addressed to his current employer and says he works at the Dolac market stall
T6: Turning the 2nd place at a county fair into an award-winning or national-level claim

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Tomislav Mesarić
Ulica Lipa 12, 10000 Zagreb, Croatia
+385 1 555 0142 | tomislav.mesaric@example.com
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Vocationally trained butcher with experience in family-shop and market meat counters. Skilled in
cutting and portioning beef, pork and lamb, advising customers, FIFO stock rotation and HACCP
temperature checks. Serves about 120 customers on Saturdays and has trained two apprentices in safe
knife handling and cleaning routines.
EXPERIENCE
Butcher | Mesnica Kod Ante, Zagreb | 2019–present
• Break down 2–3 beef forequarters and 10–12 pork sides weekly; bone, trim and portion meat for the
service counter.
• Rotate cold-room stock every morning using FIFO, placing the oldest stock at the front.
• Record cold-room temperatures (0–4 °C) and display-counter checks twice daily.
• Serve about 120 customers on a Saturday, advising on cuts and cooking times; wrap purchases in
paper.
• Make four varieties of fresh sausage, producing about 40 kg weekly in the busy season. Developed
the lamb merguez recipe and adjusted the ćevapi mix following customer feedback; the ćevapi won
second place at the Zagreb County craft meat fair in 2023.
• Train two apprentices in knife handling and cleaning routines.
Counter Assistant | Tržnica Dolac meat hall stall, Zagreb | 2015–2019
• Served customers, weighed and priced orders, operated the till and completed cash-up.
• Cleaned and sanitised slicers, mincers and the counter at closing; wrote a one-page closing and
cleaning checklist in 2017.
EDUCATION AND CERTIFICATES
Vocational certificate: Butcher, three-year programme | Food Trades School Zagreb | 2015
HACCP basic food hygiene certificate | 2021; renewed 2024
Master butcher exam (majstorski ispit) | In preparation; exam planned for spring 2027
SKILLS
Meat cutting and portioning; beef, pork and lamb carcass breakdown; boning and trimming; sausage
making; knife sharpening; mincer and bandsaw operation; FIFO stock rotation; cold-chain temperature
checks; cleaning and sanitising; customer advice; cash handling; hand pallet jack use.
LANGUAGES
Croatian: native | English: good, including customer service | German: basic

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Tomislav Mesarić
Ulica Lipa 12, 10000 Zagreb, Croatia
+385 1 555 0142 | tomislav.mesaric@example.com
FreshCart Supermarkets
Hiring Manager, Zagreb-Jarun store
Application: Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am applying for the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant position at your Zagreb-Jarun store.
I completed my butcher training in 2015 and have worked at Mesnica Kod Ante since 2019,
following four years at the Dolac market meat counter. FreshCart’s “Ask the counter” promise
matches my daily work: helping customers choose cuts and explaining how to cook them.
At Kod Ante, I break down 2–3 beef forequarters and 10–12 pork sides each week, then bone,
trim and portion meat for the counter. On Saturdays I serve about 120 customers. I rotate
cold-room stock every morning using FIFO and record cold-room and display-counter
temperature checks twice daily. My basic HACCP food hygiene certificate was renewed in
2024, and I have trained two apprentices in knife handling and cleaning routines.
Alongside counter work, I developed our lamb merguez recipe and adjusted the ćevapi mix
after customer feedback; the ćevapi won second place at the Zagreb County craft meat fair in
2023. I am also preparing for the master butcher exam planned for spring 2027. FreshCart’s
support for colleagues preparing for this exam is particularly relevant to that preparation.
The owner of Kod Ante is retiring and closing the shop at the end of 2026. I can work early
and late shifts, but would need the early shift on Wednesdays. I would welcome a meeting to
discuss how my cutting, customer service and food hygiene experience could contribute to
your counter team.
Kind regards,
Tomislav Mesarić

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
